We often hear about "prayer warriors," those who are continuously in prayer, especially for others. Who seek the burdens of others to bring them before the Lord, and it is a wonderful work.

But as we seek to be counted among the elite forces of prayer, we should always keep in mind the humility and confession that makes our prayer life effective.

And so when David writes *be merciful unto me: heal my soul; for I have sinned against thee*, we need to take it to heart in our own approach to the Throne. The man who was the apple of God's eye was honest in his confession. The King of Israel was lowly enough to be convicted as he approached the Throne of Grace.

Watch out for the creeping pride that may come from being recognized as a "prayer warrior," and the audacity that may infect what is a great habit. The loss of the love of others that should drive it, but iniquity creeping in.

Begin with confession. A contrite heart with love unfeigned can move mountains.

teachings.title: Many are the afflictions of the righteous
teachings.summary: God's commandments are for our good and He provides for His own, yet the godly will suffer affliction that grows faith, and none who trust Him will be desolate.
teachings.text:
Those that trust in the Lord know they shall never want. We are protected from evil by a host of angels. We are given our daily bread.

**Psalms 37:25**
*I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread*.

We may not be rich, we may not be feasting on expensive meals. But the Lord will provide for his own.

And the Lord promises us that we shall have a long life with good in it if we keep ourselves from speaking lies and doing evil, and rather seek peace and pursue it. Loving our neighbors.

While the Commandments of the Lord serve to let us know that we have fallen short of His perfect ways, they are given that it be well with us. That if we follow them, we have an easier life full of blessings. They are for our benefit, not to oppress us.

We are judged by the law of Liberty, not saved by our works. But our works can benefit us in our service to God.

God's eyes are upon us and he listens for our prayers, when we walk in the truth. And he is against those who commit evil, and he chastens every son He receives.

*Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the LORD delivereth him out of them all.*

**2 Timothy 3:12**
*Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution*.

While we are promised a longer life with more blessings, we are not promised a carefree life that has no suffering. Often the suffering we experience is for our benefit to help us grow in the Lord, and to increase our faith.

Praise and obedience and calling upon the Lord, and the tribulations that we suffer, all work together for good. Because they increase our faith.

The LORD redeemeth the soul of his servants: and none of them that trust in him shall be desolate.

This is the promise given to all believers. That once we are saved we are always saved.b that we shall never be left desolate. Will never be ashamed for our trust in the Lord.

He will redeem The souls of his servants and bring us out of tribulation and into Glory, in His holy name. Amen

teachings.title: Length of days forever, and the fire that devours
teachings.summary: Those who call on the Lord are given eternal life forever, while the wicked who reject Him are swallowed up in His wrath and fire.
teachings.text:
The dominant theme of the book of Psalms is placing all your faith in God alone, to redeem, to save from danger, to exact vengeance and recompense, to be the strong tower and shield, a ready comfort, faithful to His promises, generous with His mercy and gracious in His gifts.

Trusting in the Lord for every category, especially for our eternal life.

*He asked life of thee, and thou gavest it him, even length of days for ever and ever.*

Those that have called upon the name of the Lord for salvation, who trust in His promises, are given eternal life. Forever. This is the confidence we have. The sure hope that we place our trust in.

And we trust that the wicked will be dealt with according to His perfect and holy judgment.

Just as sure as our exaltation and glory is guaranteed, that through the Lord's mercy we shall not be moved, we can know the wicked who reject Him will be swallowed up in His wrath. That His fire shall devour them, as the smoke of their torment rises forever.

Eternal life and salvation, contrasted with eternal wrath and fire.

We who trusted in Him, sing praises and worship Him. We exalt the Lord, we sing praise to His power. Amen

teachings.title: Thou art all fair, my love
teachings.summary: The bride seen without blemish pictures believers made righteous and unblameable in Christ, and the sealed garden pictures eternal security.
teachings.text:
Chapter 4 opens with an ode to the beloved bride by her lover, the bridegroom. When he looks upon her he sees her fair beauty, her eyes as doves', her hair as the flocks of wild mountain goats. Picturing her black, flowing locks as the long, black, silky hair the goats have. When a herd of these dark goats grazes and moves down a steep mountain from a distance, the flowing movement creates a visual illusion of cascading hair.

He compares her teeth to the whitest of sheep, shorn and clean and notes there are none missing, a rarity to be sure in the ancient world.

Her lips, red as scarlet thread and her speech comely. Her temples and neck and breasts and scent, perfect and without blemish.

*Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.*

The poetic nature of the song, romanticizing the couples love, could be seen as hyperbole. The aura of beauty that comes with infatuation. The perfection we see when we are caught up in our love for the other.

But, as a spiritual allegory, we see the woman, who works the field and vineyard, black skinned, is without blemish when the King looks upon her. Just as we who are saved and sanctified by faith in Christ are pure when the Lord looks upon us. Clothed in righteousness. No sin imputed upon our new man.

**2 Corinthians 5:21**
*For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.*

He has made us without blemish;

**Colossians 1:21–22**
*And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight*

Solomon's King sings passionately about his beloved; *How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse!* A sister of Israel, his spouse through their betrothal and marriage.

This is also how Jesus sees us, His beloved. We are His brothers and sisters, and spouse as a collective. Made one within the body of Christ.

**Matthew 12:50**
*For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother*.

His idealized view of us, despite our sin and despite our falling short of the glory of God, comes entirely by His love for us. That while we were sinners, Christ died for us. That He justifies the ungodly. That the Spirit quickens and seals us unto redemption.

So when Solomon compares his love to an inclosed garden, walled off, a spring shut up, barred from use by others. A fountain sealed, carrying the seal of the King, and so kept pure from pollution. In this allegory we see the promise of eternal security in Christ. We are eternally His.

The fruits of the garden are orchards, even pomegranates, and pleasant fruits, and flowers and spices used in ointments and perfume. Spikenard, the precious Himalayan plant, used to anoint Christ;

**Mark 14:3**
*And being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard very precious; and she brake the box, and poured it on his head.*

The odors of her garden are pleasing. Precious to the King.  Just as our fruit, our good works in Christ, are pleasing to Him.

*A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon*. He views us and the works we do for Him the same way, and we issue forth the living waters of the Spirit when we walk in His ways.

The chapter ends shifting to the beloved woman, the bride, calling upon her lord to enter her garden, *that the spices thereof may flow out.* Spiritually, calling upon the name of the Lord, that one may be saved, that God may eat His pleasant fruits.

teachings.title: Remaining in the congregation of the dead
teachings.summary: Those who see the way of truth but reject it without truly believing are given over by God to a reprobate mind and cannot be brought again to repentance.
teachings.text:
*The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.*

**1 John 2:19**
*They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.*

**Hebrews 6:4-8** 
*For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame. For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.*

**John 6:64-65**
*But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who should betray him.*

**Proverbs 21:16** is another proof text for the understanding of the reprobate doctrine. The knowledge that a man who wandered out of the way of understanding remains in the congregation of the dead.

Notice it isn't that the person HAS understanding. They are not perfect in their ways. They saw the path, maybe followed it for a while, and left it. They tasted of the Spirit, but rejected it without ingesting, without being indwelled. They never fully believe. And when they reject the truth of God? God gives them up and gives them over. It is impossible for them to come to the knowledge of the truth. To be brought again to repentance.

**Romans 1:21-22**
*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools*

These people knew the truth, but did not glorify Him. They knew the gift, but weren't thankful for it. Their foolish heart was darkened. Hardened. They were waxed fat, dull of hearing. Eyes that could not see.

*Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts...Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections...And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient*.

They are given over to Satan. Reprobate concerning the faith. Clouds without water, twice-dead, branches cut off for unfruitfulness, cast into the fire. Conscience seared.

They remain in the congregation of the dead.

teachings.title: Turn yourselves and live
teachings.summary: Ezekiel 18's call to turn concerns national judgment and chastening, not eternal salvation, which cannot be lost.
teachings.text:
As for the use of this to teach "repent of your sins" for salvation, we understand that this is in the context of a nation being judged. While God's judgment is upon the wicked, and His mercy is upon those that walk in His ways, the wrath upon a people is based on their nation's sin. He will spare the righteous from His wrath. That's a promise.

**1 Thessalonians 5:9**
*For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ*

**Romans 5:8-9**
*But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him*.

And here, in Ezekiel's day, God is reserving a righteous remnant that would survive, and thrive, under captivity.

The assumption is that if they are walking in His ways and keeping His precepts, they are doing so by faith. **Ezekiel 1**8 encourages that commitment. The need for it in saved people.

Note the warning to the backslidden is their death along with the unrighteous. But we know that judgment is just, but not eternal, because once saved always saved. God will take a backslidden Christian home in chastisement. So we should have a certain fearful looking over the shoulder when we seek to sin.

*Cast away from you all your transgressions, whereby ye have transgressed; and make you a new heart and a new spirit: for why will ye die, O house of Israel? For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith the Lord God: wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye.*

teachings.title: The mark on the foreheads
teachings.summary: God's mark on the righteous in Ezekiel 9 is what the beast's mark copies, but God has sealed us with the Spirit unto redemption.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Ezekiel 9**, the prophet is still being given a vision of Jerusalem, filled with abominations. Some secret, some open and flagrant. Where the people say the Lord had forsaken the earth, or that He seeth not.

And the Lord, come down from the mercy seat, to the threshold of the temple, orders an angel with an inkhorn to set a mark the foreheads of the men who wept and sighed over the abominations in their midst. A righteous remnant.

Those that had charge over the city, the 6 men the Lord summons with their weapons of destruction, I believe angels of the city that kept watch over it. And He orders them to fill the courtyard of the temple with the dead, slaying utterly the old, young, maids and little children that have not the mark.

Of course, Satan has his counterfeit mark;

**Revelation 13:16**
*And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads*

And he orders those that will not worship the beast and his image, and take the mark be killed, making war with the saints. Martyring those who have the testimony of Christ.

This is what the beast is copying. But God has sealed us with the Spirit unto redemption. And those 144K that will come during the wrath will be likewise sealed. God protects His own, while the beast will damn many to torment in the time to come and eternity.

Our Lord will not forsake us. Amen

teachings.title: Delivered and translated into the kingdom
teachings.summary: Colossians 1 shows God has already delivered, redeemed and reconciled believers the moment they believed, so we should be thankful and extend that grace to others.
teachings.text:
**Colossians 1:9-15**
*For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding; That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God; Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness; Giving thanks unto the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son: In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins*

Be thankful that God has already done so much for us that have been justified in Christ, while we were yet sinners.

God has already made us *partakers of the inheritance of the saints*, *delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son*, and so, *we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins*.

As in verse 20-21; *having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven. And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled*

We are now reconciled, having made peace with the Father through the blood of the Son.

This is the good news, the glory of the Gospel of God. All of these promises have been fulfilled already, the moment you believed and received the baptism of the Spirit, quickening your spirit and sealing you into redemption.

*As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him.*

Amen. Let us give glory to the Lord Jesus for this, and to God the Father for having the grace and mercy towards us that all these things have been predestined for those who place their trust in Christ.

Knowing this peace and forgiveness and reconciliation, knowing this grace and mercy, let us extend it to our brothers, and to others that they know of our conversion, and hear the gospel on which we stand by faith.

Amen

teachings.title: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief
teachings.summary: We have the Spirit and scripture rather than signs, yet may ask God to increase our faith, and walking in the light and confessing sin gives us confidence that He hears us.
teachings.text:
Hezekiah asked for a sign that the word of God spoken of Isaiah was true. Paul writes in **1 Corinthians 1**:**22-24**;

*For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom: but we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumblingblock, and unto the Greeks foolishness; but unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.*

In the Old Testament, the Hebrews often asked for a sign, and were given them. Sometimes, God offered a sign that they may know His word was true. But we have the Spirit testifying within us, and the more sure words of prophecy of the Bible.

In our life, when we are praying to God to deliver us from bad things, illness, family members in trouble, whatever, we are reassured by the Spirit confirming the word of God and His promises to us. That according to His will, He is faithful to deliver us. This is sign enough.

But often we need more. As the tearful father said to Jesus, asking Him to bring back his daughter unto him, *Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.* Or as the apostles said to Christ, *Lord, Increase our faith.*

We can ask God for reassurance. We can ask for things we've hoped for, and see the work of the Spirit bringing it about. Increasing our faith. Helping our unbelief. It doesn't mean we doubt our salvation, or that God can't deliver. It just means we are human, and the flesh fears.

This is why it is important to be in good standing with the Father, as Hezekiah was. Able to go before God to ask of Him what we need. By walking 3the Spirit and being right with the things of God, our faith is made stronger, and our trust in him when we are weak will come more naturally.

But when we are in sin, and ashamed, and walk in the flesh, our doubts and fears increase. Our faith that God will save us falters, knowing we don't deserve His mercy.

Thankfully, He is faithful to us, that if we turn to Him, and confess our sins, He will forgive us. **1 John 1:5-9**

*This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all. If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.*

**1 John 5:13-15**
*These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God. And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him.*

So, like Hezekiah, let us walk in the light that we may have confidence in the Lord to deliver us from our troubles.

teachings.title: Secret sin and the Father's rod
teachings.summary: God chastens His adopted children and brings secret sins to light, and the guilt of conscience should drive the believer to confess and forsake sin.
teachings.text:
Of course, David takes Bathsheba as his wife, one of many. He lives with his sin and the poor decisions he has made. But the Lord is displeased and David's actions won't remain hidden for long.

**Hebrews 12:6-7**
*For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?*

**Hebrews 10:26-27**
*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.*

That fearful looking for judgment, the guilt we feel when we disobey God's word, the pangs of our conscience, is a powerful motivation to get right with the Lord. To call out to Christ our redeemer for forgiveness, to repent of our actions and seek to do the right thing. Especially knowing that, as adopted children, our Father will not spare the rod, and the sins we do in secret will be revealed in the light.

**Psalms 90:8**
*Thou hast set our iniquities before thee, our secret sins in the light of thy countenance.*

**Proverbs 28:13**
*He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy*.

**Luke 8:17**
*For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.*

teachings.title: Thou shalt not oppress him
teachings.summary: As Israel was not to return an escaped servant, the church must not hold a repentant brother's past sins against him, since we too were bondmen in Egypt.
teachings.text:
*Thou shalt not deliver unto his master the servant which is escaped from his master unto thee: He shall dwell with thee, even among you, in that place which he shall choose in one of thy gates, where it liketh him best: thou shalt not oppress him.*

This statute to defend those escaped from servitude seems straightforward but counterintuitive, but remember they were in bondage in Egypt, set free by the Lord. The same grace and mercy should be shown.

The spiritual application here then, in that context, should really strike home. It was a discussion in our chat last night. When a brother or sister in Christ comes into your congregation, their past bondage should not be held against them. Their sins are as forgiven as yours. *Thou shall not oppress him.*

This stands with those already among us and their turning from sins, even sins that may have seen them removed from church, such as drunkenness or fornication. If they have repented, and asked to be forgiven, we are to treat them as if they'd never sinned. It's not on us to remind them or judge them on those things they've left behind. For we were once bondmen in Egypt.

teachings.title: The work of the Holy Ghost
teachings.summary: The Holy Ghost quickens, indwells, comforts and seals believers unto redemption, bears witness that they are God's children, reproves the world, teaches the word and makes intercession.
teachings.text:
The Spirit of God, the Holy Ghost, which was foretold by the prophets who were moved by Him to receive the word of God, inspired, and promised of Christ Jesus to us, the Comforter. That He may dwell within us, the Father and the Son, in the Spirit. Who quickens our dead spirit, our stoney heart, and makes us live again. Who comforts us in tribulations. Who seals us as His own, the earnest of our inheritance in Christ;

**Ephesians 4:30**
*And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.*

**Ephesians 1:13-14**
*In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

This is the promise, that we who are saved may know we are His, and that we know we have eternal life, adopted as joint-heirs, made sons of God;

**Romans 8:16**
*The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God*.

We who the Spirit indwells are given the power to free those we share the truth with from their sins, to be born again of the Spirit as we were. Through the Gospel, which is given by the Spirit of Truth, that by hearing the inspired word of God, they may believe, and by faith be saved, that they may save others in His name, by that same Spirit. Or, if they have not the Spirit of truth, to be condemned, opposing themselves. Anathema.

All men are called by the Spirit, God the Father having lifted up the Son, because the Spirit of the Comforter works to reproved the world of sin, righteousness and judgment. That they may know they need salvation, and believe.

And all knowledge is given by the Holy Ghost, who teaches us all things, making God's word understandable, as we hear His voice and follow Him. And bringing all things to remembrance, that we may be able to give a ready answer for the hope we have in Him.

And by making our prayers effectual, even as we in our sin don't know what we need, the Spirit makes intercession for us before God in Christ's name.

teachings.title: Repentance is metanoia, not turning from sin
teachings.summary: Repentance is a change of mind that brings discernment, and turning from sin follows only if the new man is fed, while the backslider is still saved.
teachings.text:
Repentance, or metanoia, having a change of heart, coming to a new understanding that is (by grace, led of the Spirit); discernment.

We gain discernment regarding the will of God and the state of ourselves and man in relation to Him, when we repent. When we believe the scriptures that say God would offer a sacrifice of His own making to free us from death and Hell. That that sacrifice is the Son of God, Jesus Christ.

That discernment, if the new man created at salvation is fed, leads to a change in attitude towards sin. It becomes less desirable. The lusts of the flesh can lose their appeal. Even disgusting us.

If that new man isn't fed, and they continue walking in the flesh, they are still saved by the knowledge of the truth, but that discernment is dulled and God may have to chasten the person to work godly sorrow in their heart. If they remain backslidden, God may call them home.

But they are still saved.

Saying "real repentance WILL mean you turn from sin, and WILL walk in the Spirit," is false. We must pick up our cross daily. It is a choice to engage in sanctification. But salvation is of Christ, not ourselves. It is by grace, not of ourselves.

teachings.title: The fruits of the Spirit are not automatic
teachings.summary: Even Paul struggled with sin, so good works and victory over sin are a daily choice to walk in the Spirit, and when we fall we confess and are forgiven.
teachings.text:
And just one more point that I've touched on here but needs to seriously be stressed; the fruits of the Spirit don't come automatically.. Just because we are saved doesn't mean that we will do good. Just as it doesn't mean we will stop sinning.

Paul, who many consider the greatest Christian of all time for his understanding of God's word, writes of himself here in Romans chapter 7;

*But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.*

Writing in **1 Timothy 1:15**
*This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.*

Paul and the other authors of the epistles write to be edifying to the brethren, that they *should* do good, that they *should not* do evil. That we *should* walk in the spirit that we do not fulfill the lusts of the flesh.

This is a choice. As Jesus says;

**Luke 9:23**
*And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.*

It's a daily choice. It is on us to reject the temptations of the flesh by walking in the spirit.

But it is not automatic. Even Paul struggled with sin.

So many people beat themselves up for failing to stop sin in their life. For falling short. But what does the Bible tells us? That all fall short.

**1 John 1:9**
*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

And so we are instructed; *Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.*

And when we stumble, confess to God who has adopted us as sons, and He will forgive us and help us with our infirmities.

Don't allow the men of this world to judge your walk, and in doing so place stumbling blocks and snares for you. Those hypocrites have their reward. Instead, every day make a commitment to walk in the spirit, do for others, what you can. And give glory to God for His righteousness and mercy, in Christ Jesus. The rest will sort itself out.

teachings.title: The man to whom the Lord imputeth not sin
teachings.summary: Repentance from dead works to faith in God saves by faith alone, and God promises not to impute sin to the believer but to remember it no more.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 6:1**
*Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God*

Repentance from dead works and to faith towards God. Turning from means turning towards. From trusting in our works of righteousness to faith in God. This is the foundation that is built on the rock that is Christ.

And so, reckoned of faith, the man who does no works but believes, is saved by that faith alone. Paul quotes Davin from **Psalm 32**
*Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, Whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man unto whom the LORD imputeth not iniquity, And in whose spirit there is no guile*.

The Lord will not impute sin, our ledger is clean, our transgressions forgiven.

For what is sin?

**1 John 3:4**
*Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.*

But we who believe not only are forgiven of sins past, but God will not impute sin to us. Our transgression is forgiven. This is a promise of God.

**Hebrews 10:17**
*And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

teachings.title: Good person, mass and purgatory cope
teachings.summary: Those trusting works claim to be good people yet call assurance presumption and invent purgatory, because they will not admit they are sinners deserving Hell.
teachings.text:
Talk with them, soul winning and even online, and they will say they know they are going to heaven because they are a "good person," or that they attend mass and take communion and go to confession. But in the back of their mind they know this isn't true, that they imperfectly follow the law of God, and even fall short of the traditions of man. And so they will hedge by saying it is presumption to claim to know if you're saved. That they "think so, but God decides at judgment." That unbiblical things like purgatory exist as a Plan B is a testament to the cope people will cling to to deny that they are sinners deserving death and Hell.

And the Gospel reminds them of this, triggers them, and their anger has resulted in persecution and murder of martyrs, just as the prophets slain in the OT times. Just as it did Christ. Just as it did the apostles and the early church and through the dark ages.

Man doesn't want to humble themselves to the truth of their nature and what they deserve. They seek reassurance that they are good. That they deserve salvation.

But we know this isn't true.

teachings.title: Thyatira Suffered That Woman Jezebel to Teach
teachings.summary: Thyatira's troubles came from suffering a woman to teach against 1 Timothy 2:12, and Christ chastens such backslidden servants severely though they are saved.
teachings.text:
*And unto the angel of the church in Thyatira write; These things saith the Son of God, who hath his eyes like unto a flame of fire, and his feet are like fine brass;*

Again, writing now to Thyatira, Jesus as described in John's vision.

*I know thy works, and charity, and service, and faith, and thy patience, and thy works; and the last to be more than the first.*

The church at Thyatira is doing well, their works growing, the last more than the first. Patient, charitable, serving others, faithful.

*Notwithstanding I have a few things against thee, because thou sufferest that woman Jezebel, which calleth herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants to commit fornication, and to eat things sacrificed unto idols.*

But the Thyatirians have multiple problems, that all stem from allowing, suffering, a woman to teach.

**1 Timothy 2:12**:
*But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.*

We see here exactly why this is a problem. Jezebel is joy only teaching, but in the authority she's gained over the men, has seduced them into fornication and to eat things sacrificed to idols. The error of Balaam compounded by her role in their church.

*And I gave her space to repent of her fornication; and she repented not. Behold, I will cast her into a bed, and them that commit adultery with her into great tribulation, except they repent of their deeds. And I will kill her children with death; and all the churches shall know that I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts: and I will give unto every one of you according to your works.*

By this passage, I assume Jezebel is actually a saved believer. That the sin she is in and leading others too comes from their disobeying God's word, and compounding the error, when given chance to repent and turn back towards God, she refused. Backslidden and defiant, Jesus says He will punish her and those who are with her. He chasteneth who He loves. These aren't some sort of reprobates like the Nicolaitanes, these are His servants gone astray.

And the punishment is severe. Casting her into bed, stricken sick. Likely of STDs. And those she misled into great tribulation, until they repent. He will even kill her children that the other churches will know the error that they were in, and His power, giving to each what they deserve that others may learn from their folly. We should all heed this warning, God is longsuffering but has His limits. He will repay us by our works, here on earth, even if we have been saved from Hell.

*But unto you I say, and unto the rest in Thyatira, as many as have not this doctrine, and which have not known the depths of Satan, as they speak; I will put upon you none other burden.*
*But that which ye have already hold fast till I come.* 

Jesus says to the rest of the congregation that haven't fallen into this wickedness to holdfast. Encouraging them that He will honor His promises to us at His return.

*And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father. And I will give him the morning star. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.*

We who are saved and keep to His commands, doing the works He has asked of us, we will be rewarded by ruling and reigning over the Earth with Him in the millennial Kingdom. Ruling with a rod of iron, the perfect law of God. And we will receive the morning star, the glory that is Christ Jesus. Amen.

teachings.title: Have faith in God and forgive when ye pray
teachings.summary: God promises to answer believing prayer, but we must forgive others as He forgave us, since unforgiveness hinders us and God chastens disobedient sons on earth.
teachings.text:
*Have faith in God.*

*For verily I say unto you, That whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that those things which he saith shall come to pass; he shall have whatsoever he saith. Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.*

This is not simply an affirmation to put on Instagram. It's not just a "hang in there, God provides" pick me up for a daily inspirational devotion.

It is a promise from God. All He asks is your forgiveness for others as He has forgiven you. To not hold grudges. To let things that aren't important in this life, and keep you from earning the rewards of the next, to let them go.

*When ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses. But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father which is in heaven forgive your trespasses.*

Now, all our sin is forgiven and forgotten in Christ Jesus, at judgment. All believers are in the Book of Life, and so saved.

But on earth, God still punishes the disobedient believers, His chastisement falls on those He loves.

*For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?*

*But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.*

And we are to confess our sins to God asking for forgiveness;

*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

But how can we humble ourselves to ask for forgiveness for disobeying God when we hold back forgiveness from those who've wronged us? Forgive our trespasses as we forgive others is part of the model for prayer Jesus provides.

Lack of forgiveness is a burden. In the same measure we give mercy and extend grace, the Bible says, is what we receive.

Be mindful of this, and in faith unfeigned, without the burdens of hate and a lack of grace, go boldly before God with your needs. And the Lord God, who cannot lie, promises He will provide.

teachings.title: God is just, and God is love
teachings.summary: Scoffers who call God cruel for damning imperfect men are fruit of works religion, but God saves by grace through faith all who believe, as a gift that can never be lost.
teachings.text:
A common refrain of the worldly scoffers that God is "cruel," and "how can a just God sens us to Hell knowing we can't be perfect?"

This ignorance is the bad fruit of the damnable heresies of works-based religions that teach we must earn our way to Heaven, that our own righteousness keeps us from Hell.

There are none righteous no not one. The wages of sin is death. *But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.*

*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.*

God is just. God is love. And He gave us the hope in Christ, that all who believe on Jesus are saved. Just as we are, *sealed unto the day of redemption.* Everlasting life, given as a gift, that can never be lost or taken away. Regardless of our own righteousness, which the Bible says are filthy rags.

*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the GIFT OF GOD: Not of works, lest any man should boast.*

Even *to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.*

As Jesus, who cannot lie said; *And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.*

*My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand.*

*I and my Father are one.*

If you have been one of those who felt lost and hopeless because you were told God only saves the righteous, and that if you become Christian, you have to be perfect or face Hell, understand that this is not what the Bible teaches. That there is hope. That God's grace is unto you in Christ just as you are.

teachings.title: I never knew you
teachings.summary: Depart from me, I never knew you proves no saved person loses salvation, and the will of the Father is that whoever sees the Son and believes on Him has everlasting life.
teachings.text:
And thinking themselves righteous, when they come before Jesus touting their works, he says depart from me I never knew you. (Proving you don't lose salvation. He doesn't say he used to know them, but never did)

In verses 21-23, Jesus lays in to those selfish and vain workers of iniquity, but many unsaved people trapped in false doctrine twist this verse to mean you must do works to be saved. "You must do the will of the Father see!"

But what is the will of the Father? Jesus tells us;

*This is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

We are building our house upon the solid rock of the word. Living the sayings of scripture, embodied in Christ. Doing the will of the Father.

Those who ignore scripture, rely on shifting traditions of man and their ever-changing doctrines, are building upon sand.

teachings.title: I am the vine, ye are the branches
teachings.summary: The fruit of John 15 is souls won, and a fruitless believer is set aside from usefulness, not cast into hell, for the passage speaks to the saved about service.
teachings.text:
A slight continuation of John chapter 14, Jesus is giving His saved followers final instructions, calling on them to win souls for God. The fruit they bear are converted and saved Christians, who like a branch of a vine then produce more fruit, and so on. Branching out and on, one long vine back to Him, the true vine.

God the Father being the husbandman, the planter of the vine, the one who receives the fruit.

We are called as Christians to be *meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work.* To live in the word, reading scripture, in prayer, sanctified, abiding in Christ so that we may be able to bring forth that fruit.

If we don't, if we stay carnal, stay in the flesh, not living in Christ but instead the world, we become useless. Withered and dead, producing no fruit. And God "fires" us.

Some take this verse out of context to say that we can lose our salvation and that we are cast to Hell, but every mention of fire isn't about Hell. Rightly dividing the word of God often comes down to knowing if it's being addressed to saved or unsaved, about salvation or about another topic. This is one of those cases.

We should glorify the Father by being soul winning examples, bearing much fruit. Being Christ's disciples. Not all saved believers rise to this. In fact few do.

These are the commandments mentioned in v10, the preceding 9 verses. Not the 10 commandments, but being worthy Christians bearing fruit. It's specific context to the chapter.

teachings.title: The Son honoured as the Father
teachings.summary: Jesus teaches His authority comes from the Father, that the Godhead are three persons yet one, and that whoever hears and believes hath everlasting life and shall not come into condemnation.
teachings.text:
The remaining verses of the chapter are all red letter preaching by Jesus.

Jesus establishes His sonship with the Father. That He emulates and gets His authority from the Father. That His dominion as the Son is the authority of the Father, and to honor the Father you must honor Jesus.

This is pure doctrine.

Next Jesus again gives the good news of the Gospel; Saying He is telling us truthfully that any who hear God's word, His testimony of Christ, and believe, **has** everlasting life and **shall not** come I to condemnation. (Again showing that once we are saved it is forever. We HAVE everlasting life. We WON'T be condemned)

Jesus preaches that the dead in spirit will hear His voice, His word, and live. Salvation quickens, or makes alive, our dead spirit inside and brings us into life.

Jesus says not to marvel at the basic Gospel, just wait until the resurrection of the dead!

Jesus again teaches He is not there for His own will, but that of the Father. Each member of the Godhead has His own will, are their own person, Father, the Son and the Spirit. But these three are one and obey the will of God the Father.

Jesus accuses the Jews of not believing the witness of those testifying He is Christ and what He says is true. He points to John the Baptist as one, then the Holy Ghost, the works of God the Father Jesus does, and the very scriptures that the Pharisees claim their authority from, that testifies to who Jesus is.

The Jews claim to believe in the resurrection of the dead and the salvation of the Christ, but they don't have the truth in them, and so they can't see it when He's literally in front of them.
